macros.doc: The command \coloredlines causes \plotdata to use the rendering command \draw with a color option that cycles through eight different colors starting with black (hey! black is a color too).

macros.name: hypergeodesic

macros.name: makesector
macros.doc: The modifying macro \makesector can be applied to any path, but its name makes sense (and its action is predictable) only if that path is an arc. It appends line segments from the center of the arc’s circle to the ends of the arc, producing a closed path.

macros.name: mfpdataperline
macros.doc: When MFPIC is reading from data files and writing to the output file, this macro stores the maximum number of data points that will be written on a single line in the output file.

macros.doc: This skip register (‘rubber length’ in LaTeX) stores the space between a picture and the caption produced with \tcaption.

macros.name: mfpicunit

macros.name: mfpuntil

macros.name: pointedlines
macros.doc: The command \pointedlines causes \plotdata to use the rendering command \plot, cycling through nine symbols.

macros.name: polygon

macros.doc: Initially, MFPIC uses the \draw command (stroking) as the default operation when a figure is to be rendered. However, this can be changed to any combination of MFPIC rendering commands or indeed any TeX commands, by using the \setrender command.

macros.name: settension

macros.name: usepic

envs.name: tile
envs.doc: In this environment, all drawing commands contribute to a tile. A tile is a rectangular picture which may be used to fill the interior of closed paths.
